speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand the connection between your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, how would you describe the nature of your vision loss—does it worsen when you look up? Also, do you experience any trouble swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Anti-MuSK antibodies, Anti-AChR antibodies, and Repetitive Nerve Stimulation. Do you notice your symptoms fluctuate significantly throughout the day, becoming worse as you get more tired?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is surprising, as tuberculosis does not typically present with fluctuating weakness or specific ocular motility issues like the double vision you described. Given the pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, could you tell me if you experience significant fatigue or difficulty speaking clearly? Also, do you have any history of myasthenia gravis or Lambert-Eaton syndrome?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies and MuSK Antibodies
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain and Cervical Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated), MuSK_Antibodies: Not Detected, MRI_Brain: Normal, MRI_Cervical_Spine: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, combined with your symptoms of fatigable muscle weakness and ocular diplopia, confirms this diagnosis. The normal MRI rules out structural causes, and the lack of MuSK antibodies aligns with the classic AChR-positive presentation.
